text.text_excerpt: This was my first Jazz fest and I was so privileged to attend their 50th anniversary. I call it "1st and 50". We planned this trip way in advance and I was anxiously waiting to go to New Orleans as almost all my friends who had been to New Orleans told me that they have arguably the best food in US. The tickets for Jazz fest are $75 per day. Opens at 11am and closes at 7pm. Various stages host bands all day long. They have a nice app that you can download to check their schedule. So add a reminder on your phone if you see your favorite band and try to go their at least 10 mins before the start as you can grab nice seats. Almost all the shows started on time. So that was very good. I saw D...

A perfect experience. Endless amazing music from different genres at multiple stages, huge selection of any type of food you could possibly want (hellooooo crawfish Monica), and a great freakin atmosphere. Jazz fest 2016 was perfect. Everyone listening to good music, having a good time, indulging in some fabulous Cajun or creole cuisine. Nothing better. Let the good times roll indeed!! Did notice that as the day progressed the festival became wayyyyyy too crowded. I think they need to get their ish together and figure out a way to handle this as it's honestly a safety hazard.

This was my first year going, and it was everything you expect it to be. Lots of great food options, lots of great music, and hot dusty air. But overall, I LOVE Jazz Fest. It was so much fun! As with all food fairs, if you have food concerns, your best bet would be to eat before and after going. You are allowed one bottle of water in to the grounds, so be sure to use it, and refill it at that lone water station. I figured out that I like bringing a blanket to sit on while waiting for the next act, and finding that lone tree to sit under. Don't forget your shades and hat.
